verdict.rationale: Solid provides strong architectural support for scaling (fine-grained reactivity avoiding needless re-renders, built-in Context/Stores instead of external state libs, SSR/streaming, functions-as-components enabling clean code organization) and has real-world corroboration of large-app use (Asciinema rewrite, a reported 'largish web product' used for over a year) plus benchmark evidence of speed/size at scale. However, multiple hands-on reports flag maintainability friction at scale: inconsistent naming conventions, ecosystem gaps (Framer Motion, trpc/tanstack-query), alpha-quality devtools, and specific slow/unworkable areas like SolidStart routing and Suspense — all bearing directly on 'stay maintainable as codebase grows'. missing for 10: independent large-scale case studies with team-size details, and resolution of the noted devtools/ecosystem maturity gaps.
